data.name: Anjanish
data.gender_notes: Anjanish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word Anjana, meaning 'Goddess Anjani'. Anjanish is a name of great joy and delight, evoking images of the divine mother's love and nurturing care. The name Anjanish carries the meaning “Goddess Anjani's Delight” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anjanish usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess anjani's delight and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine grace and protection of Goddess Anjani, bestowing upon the bearer courage, strength, and wisdom.
data.etymology: Anjanish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess Anjani's Delight.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anjanish total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Anjanish holds a significant place in Hindu mythology, representing divine motherhood and nurturing love. The name is derived from Anjani, the Hindu goddess who is known for her unwavering love and dedication towards her son, Lord Hanuman. The name is a celebration of the power and strength of maternal love, a value deeply cherished in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Anjanish serves as a reminder of the unconditional love and care of the Divine Mother. It symbolizes the idea that even in times of hardship and struggle, the Mother (God) is always there, nurturing and supporting us like a loving mother would. The name evokes a sense of peace, comfort, and protection, and is an inspiring reminder of the boundless love and compassion that exists within us all.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Anjanish is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Anjana', which means 'mother of Lord Hanuman'. This name is believed to bestow the blessings and strength of Hanuman, symbolizing courage, devotion, and unwavering loyalty.

historical_references.reference: Anjanisi is mentioned as a sage in the epic Mahabharata, who was a disciple of sage Vyasa and was present during the recitation of the Mahabharata.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It mainly consists of a narrative of the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and the Kaurava princes, with the Bhagavad Gita as a part of it.

historical_references.reference: Anjaneya, another form of Anjanish, is the name of the vanara general and principal devotee of Lord Rama. He is most famously known for bringing Lord Rama's wife, Sita, back from Lanka after she was abducted by Ravana.
historical_references.context: Ramayana is an ancient Indian epic that is one of the two major Sanskrit epics, the other being the Mahabharata. It tells the story of Prince Rama, who embarks on a journey to rescue his wife Sita, who has been abducted by King Ravana.
